parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The electrons each have charge $-q$ and drift speed $v$ in the slice.

State the magnitude and the direction of the force due to the magnetic field on each electron as it enters the slice.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The force on the electrons causes a voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ to be established across the semiconductor slice given by the expression

$$V_{\text{H}} = \frac{BI}{ntq}$$

where $I$ is the current in the slice.
parts.text: State the two faces between which the voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ is established.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use letters from Fig. 8.1 to identify the distance $t$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Aluminium ($^{27}_{13}\text{Al}$) has a density of $2.7 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$. Assume that there is one free electron available to carry charge per atom of aluminium.
parts.text: Show that the number of charge carriers per unit volume in aluminium is $6.0 \times 10^{28} \text{ m}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
A sample of aluminium foil has a thickness of $0.090 \text{ mm}$. The current in the foil is $4.6 \text{ A}$.

A uniform magnetic field of flux density $0.15 \text{ T}$ acts at right-angles to the foil.

Use the value in (i) to calculate the voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ that is generated.
